question: On 21 March 2024, Commissioner Jutta Urpilainen launched a new Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on inclusive and equitable societies for Latin America and the Caribbean, which will mobilise more than EUR 1 billion.

As announced by the Commission, the TEI aims to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals by developing inclusive policies in areas such as gender and social policies, care and well-being, youth, and social inclusion through quality education and access to decent jobs. This TEI could be an opportunity to advance the Bi-regional Care Pact between the European Union and Latin America and the Caribbean.

This pact, which is based on the European Care Strategy presented by the Commission in 2022 and the Buenos Aires Commitment adopted by the member states of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean in the same year, could be an essential tool to address the unequal distribution of care work between men and women in our regions. 1.
Does the Commission intend to use the TEI as an instrument to establish a roadmap for action to consolidate the Bi-regional Care Pact?
Does the Commission plan to move forward with legislation to ensure compliance with the European Care Strategy?
